recent.title: What Feeds Below
recent.author: Tatiana Schlote-Bonne
recent.review: the void is a living nightmare and somehow i STILL wanted to explore every inch of it. WHAT IS WRONG WITH ME ? 😭 i think the void itself is what made this book so memorable. it’s such a horrifying yet fascinating place , and i was obsessed with how vividly it was described. everything feels so alive and thriving in a way , from the monstrous creatures to the most unassuming little organisms that can kill you before you even realise you’re in danger. the cryptids and mutations only made it all the more unsettling. it genuinely felt like stepping into a fever dream , and i loved every second of it. and THE BODY HORROR ??? as a horror fan , i was VERY happy with how brutal some of the imagery got. the descriptions did not hold back , and i was absolutely LIVING for every horrifying detail. pair that with the pacing , where practically every chapter has SOMETHING happening , and you’ve got yourself an incredibly addictive little horror read. i also really loved our main character and her view on life. even though she definitely had her flaws , i thought she showed so much character development by the end. in a world where practically everything is trying to kill you , she’s looking at these horrifying organisms and wondering how she could turn them into medicine. there’s something so endearing about someone who can find the potential for healing in a place filled with so much death. what surprised me too was how much the story had to say about love and validation , and the lengths we’re willing to go to feel wanted. there’s this underlying question of what happens when you become so attached to someone that you start losing yourself in them. where do you draw the line between loving someone and needing them to the point where you can’t exist outside their shadow ? i thought that was a really interesting layer beneath all the chaos. now , the reason this isn’t quite a perfect read for me is the ending. while i found it sad and wished things could’ve turned out differently , the main twist was unfortunately something i’d already pieced together. some of the clues scattered throughout the story weren’t exactly subtle , so i never got that HOLY SHIT WHAT JUST HAPPENED moment i was hoping for. there’s also one particular detail about how quickly things escalated towards the end with the mutations that i'm still a little confused about. but none of that took away from how much i enjoyed the overall experience. i’m SO glad i managed to squeeze this into the final week of october despite being swamped with internship work. it was literally the perfect way to close out spooky reading month... although let’s be real , october ending is NOT going to stop me from reading horror well into november and december. SO glad i picked this up to close out my october. i’ll definitely be keeping an eye on whatever this author writes next !

recent.title: The Exquisite Torment of Loving Your Enemy (Dearly Beloathed, #2)
recent.author: Brigitte Knightley
recent.review: i need brigitte knightley to explain why watching osric and aurienne try to outsmart each other for two entire books is somehow one of the more entertaining things i've read this year. like seriously... how are they STILL finding new ways to get under each other's skin and me eating up every second of it. i don't think i've laughed this much while reading a fantasy book in a LONG time. some of the dialogue in this duology is so batshit insane that i genuinely had to stop reading just to process.. and it's not even just the main two because the side characters have some absolute GOLD too. knightley's writing style is genuinely something else and i can absolutely see why it wouldn't work for everyone , but once you get used to it , it's ridiculously entertaining. i LOVE these characters. what is it with sequels topping their predecessors recently because i really did enjoy this more than book one. there's more action , the relationship develops beautifully and THANK GOD we actually got a proper ending this time because after that cliffhanger in book one , i was NOT about to survive another round of unanswered questions. seeing everything finally come together was so satisfying and honestly , i couldn't have asked for a better ending for these two. my biggest complaint though is that i STILL wanted more from the actual fantasy plot. yes , there's definitely more happening here compared to book one , but the stakes never felt quite as high as i wanted them to. osric's seth rot was supposed to be this potentially fatal condition and such a huge part of why these characters even met , but the way it was resolved felt a little too straightforward and easy. like oh okay... it's just drastically improving now ?? 😭 i never really felt like either of them was in serious danger , and while the romantic tension was absolutely THERE , i wish the external conflicts had carried that same intensity. and that's really what keeps this from being a five-star read for me , even though i was INVESTED... like i finished this in two days and loved spending more time with these characters. my only wish is that the fantasy side was a bit more developed to match how brilliant the humor and romance were. anywayssss , four stars for two of the most insufferable people i've ever had the pleasure of reading about. i will miss these two terribly.

recent.title: Cursed City (Harker Academy, #2)
recent.author: Kate  Golden
recent.review: i would like to start this review by issuing a HUGE fucking apology to literally everyone because WHAT THE HELL WAS I THINKING WHEN I WROTE MY HALF CITY REVIEW !!!? i called myself a full reid defender. i said that man better be endgame. i said i did NOT want the other option. AT ALL. and now here i am , in full clown makeup , because apparently the ONE time i decide to abandon every single principle i have and root for the supposedly good guy instead of the villain , THIS is what happens to me ??? TEAM VILLAIN IS LITERALLY IN MY BIO. i had ONE rule and somehow i broke it for reid graveheart. i have genuinely never felt so stupid in my life. and the worst part is that i have the evidence IN WRITING. my half city review is literally sitting there for everyone to see. i was so confident too... literally my thirteenth reason. ANYWAYSS. moving on from that because HOLY SHYT KATE GOLDEN ??? i cannot even say she outdid herself because that would be an understatement. she absolutely CRUSHED this book and somehow we're only on book TWO. if you've read my half city review , you'll know that i didn't love the first book nearly as much as i wanted to. i liked it , but the pacing dragged and there was so much setup that i kept wishing things would just MOVE. well apparently kate golden heard every single complaint i had because cursed city took everything i wanted from book one and delivered it about a BILLION times better. the pacing was incredible , the twists had me losing my mind and THE CHARACTER DEVELOPMENT. THE DRAMA ?!! everything was just SO much better this time around. and VIV !!! the amount of growth this girl has shown since half city is insane. she's come such a long way and i loved seeing different sides of her this time around. the way i switched sides for deacon practically gave me whiplash. i am officially and unapologetically team mr white antlers now and i would like everyone to kindly forget every single thing i have ever said about his brother. thank yeww. also , we NEED to talk about how emotionally exhausting this book was because there were moments where i genuinely had to PUT IT DOWN. not because i was bored , but because i could feel things going horribly wrong and needed to save myself from whatever emotional damage was coming next. except that did not last before i picked it right back up because this book was so ridiculously addictive. THAT ENDING too. i don't think i've screamed at a book this much in a LONG time. sooo we're getting an underworld arc in book three. AN UNDERWORLD / HELL ARC. as someone who absolutely LIVES for dante's inferno and anything involving hell , you have NO idea how excited i am. the possibilities are actually making me feral. i already KNOW the final book might somehow top this one and that is INSANE considering how much i loved this one. fairyloot doing a matching edition is literally everything to me because FINALLY my half city won't be sitting there looking pretty alone. don't even get me started on the bookish box reverse dust jacket because THAT is the deacon graveheart i pictured in my head the whole time. absolutely no regrets about needing both editions now. five stars. the easiest five stars. i am SO unbelievably happy i continued this series because this was everything i wanted and so much more. kate golden has officially made me completely obsessed with this trilogy and i will be FIRST IN LINE for book three. july cannot come any faster. i NEED IT. 😭

recent.title: Murder at the Grand Alpine Hotel
recent.author: Lucy Foley
recent.review: murder at the grand alpine hotel had agatha christie’s name on the cover and somehow still had me waiting for the actual murder mystery to START for half the book. like i’m sorry but what are we doing here 😭 i went into this expecting a clever murder mystery with plenty of twists and turns. instead , what i got felt more like a cozy fantasy with a little murder mystery sprinkled on top. and i KNOW some people are going to think i’m insane for saying this but i genuinely would not consider this a thriller. SO much of this book is just character drama and people talking to each other. which isn’t necessarily a bad thing because i actually enjoyed the alternating POVs and getting to see the different character dynamics play out. but when practically nothing happens for the first 50% of a murder mystery , we’ve got a problem. my biggest complaint though is the investigation itself. for something involving miss marple , i expected a LOT more cleverness. instead , it felt like the book was deliberately withholding information from the reader just so everything could be explained at the very end. and i’m sorry but having characters sit around explaining how they figured everything out is nowhere near as satisfying as actually watching an investigation unfold. i wanted to connect the dots WITH the characters , not have the answers handed to me after the fact. it just made the entire payoff feel so flat. HOWEVER , i will give credit where it’s due because there were genuinely a few twists i did not see coming. i didn’t guess who was responsible for the murders and i actually really liked some of the character motivations behind everything. which makes this even more frustrating because the reveals themselves were interesting ! i just wish the journey to getting there had been equally as good. so yeah , i didn’t hate this. there were things i enjoyed and i can appreciate what the book was trying to do. but when the mystery takes half the book to properly get going and the investigation itself ends up feeling this underwhelming , i can’t help being disappointed. it was okay , just nowhere near what i was hoping for.

labels: a few twists i didn't see
